blocks.text: Condo buildings in Queen Mary Park Surrey

CLASSIFICATION CONFLICTS — FLAGGED AT THE TOP, PER THE STANDING RULE: (1) Sterling Court — a current listing places the building under "West Newton," while the building directory places it under Queen Mary Park Surrey.
The Crossing — 8115 121A Street

Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, built 1999, four storeys, frame-wood construction, with a guest suite, recreation/amenity room, clubhouse, bike room and underground parking in directory-listed amenities.
Melrose Place — 8068 120A Street

Apartment/Condo, built 1995. Listings describe it as "pet friendly Melrose Place" with guest suites and an amenities room, and note hot water and a gas fireplace included in the strata fee for the listed unit.
Sterling Court — 8142 120A Street

Apartment/Condo. YEAR CONFLICT: the directory records it built 1992, while a current listing records built 1994 and describes a "completely rainscreened building, new building envelope" — the year is carried as 1992–1994, not confirmed exact, and the rainscreen/envelope work is a listing claim to verify against the depreciation report. Directory amenities: elevator, in-suite laundry.
Eclipse — 8084 120A Street

Apartment/Condo; the name is confirmed by current listing copy ("Welcome to ECLIPSE!"), and City of Surrey Council minutes of September 25, 2006 and June 11, 2007 independently confirm a four-storey residential apartment building approved at this address — the primary-source anchor for the building.
The Birches — 8139 121A Street
Apartment/Condo; the name is confirmed by listing copy ("at The Birches!"). Listings conflict on the build year — 1994 in one record, 1995 in another — so the year is not confirmed exact.
Tamaron (The Tamaron) — 12083 92A Avenue

Apartment/Condo, built 2003. Directory-listed amenities include a club house, elevator, exercise centre, guest suite, in-suite laundry and storage. Another listing's claim that the strata contributes 20% to its CRF with a balance over $930,000 is a single-listing claim, attributed here as such and not treated as a strata fact.
Quinn by Porte (Quinn by Porte Homes) — 13439 94A Avenue and 9456 134 Street

By Porte Homes: a six-storey wood-frame mid-rise of 174 units of one- and two-bedroom-plus-den condos, completed 2024 per the project source, with listings recording it built 2024, Apartment/Condo, freehold strata. A directory header's "22-unit development" figure for the 9456 address conflicts with the 174-unit project total and is not used.
Galilea — 13458 95 Avenue

By Whitetail Homes. The developer's information sheet states 129 homes at 13458 95th Avenue and describes the project as move-in ready; listings record it built 2025, Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, six storeys. Listing-described amenities include a gym, wellness centre, party room, playground courtyard and shared workspace; a listing header records "Cats OK."
Gabriel — 13455 94A Avenue

By Whitetail Homes, the companion building to Galilea on the same 94A Avenue/95 Avenue ground. A project source states six storeys and 125 condominiums over two levels of underground parking, with completion estimated for spring 2026; current listings record it built 2026, Apartment/Condo, subdivision Gabriel, and describe units as move-in ready, and the building directory records Gabriel Condos built 2026. A listing header records "Cats OK."
Not confirmed, not counted — "Celest," said to be at 8183 121A Street
The building is therefore documented as an unnamed, uncounted building at 8183 121A Street until a directory, developer or City source confirms the name.
Another index-page address, 10721 139 Street, has no verified building name and sits at the Whalley edge — not confirmed, not counted.
Streets, schools and getting around Queen Mary Park Surrey

items.t: Queen Mary Park Surrey is a board sub-area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, named for the City park of the same name. It has no City of Surrey neighbourhood or plan-area boundary — the City does not plan it as a named neighbourhood — so its formal boundaries are not verified, and no boundary line for it should be published as fact.
That is a listing observation from one reading, not a boundary.

The sub-area sits where two City communities meet — Whalley/City Centre to the north and Newton to the south — and which City community a specific address falls in is address-specific and not verified at the area level.

Queen Mary Park itself is at 8972 Queen Mary Boulevard, north of 88 Avenue and west of 132 Street: natural trails loop the northwest portion, with a playground and the Healy Creek ecosystem. The City's park page does not list gardens, picnic areas or sports facilities for this park — wider descriptions circulating in site copy are not City facts. Bear Creek Park (13750 88 Avenue) is at the sub-area's northeast and Queen Elizabeth Meadows Park is at 9400 134 Street.

Transit frames both edges: the R1 King George Boulevard RapidBus runs along the east side and the R6 Scott Road RapidBus along Scott Road (120 Street) on the west side, both connecting to Expo Line stations — which is why the sub-area's condo clusters sit at its two edges, on 120A/121A Streets in the south and on 134 Street in the north. The planned King George Boulevard BRT would also run along the east edge.
Surrey Memorial Hospital stands at 13750 96 Avenue on the sub-area's north edge, and the Surrey-Newton Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 6830 King George Boulevard on the east side.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Queen Mary Park Surrey

items.t: In the 1990s southern cluster this report is the key document: it is where a claim like Sterling Court's "completely rainscreened, new building envelope" is either documented or not.
Pets: pet limits remain lawful strata bylaws.

Zoning and plan status: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs, under the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026). Queen Mary Park has no neighbourhood plan of its own, so there is no NCP designation sheet to quote for these buildings — any source presenting one is presenting something that does not exist.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) and suites: Surrey permits 3 units on lots under 280 m² and 4 units on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — both RapidBus edges (R1 and R6) put much of this sub-area's house stock inside a frequent-stop band. One secondary suite per house is permitted under the BC Building Code framework, and an unpermitted suite is not made legal by the SSMUH rules. That matters here because the sub-area's house listings openly describe unauthorized suites; the legality of any specific suite is per-property and not confirmed until the permits are checked.

GST on new builds is 5%. It does not apply to ordinary resales — a Quinn resale listing says so for its own unit — but it does apply to developer sales, which is the live question at Gabriel (completed 2026) and any developer-held units at Galilea and Quinn. The first-time home buyers' GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, per CRA Excise and GST/HST News No. 122) rebates 100% of the GST on a new home priced up to $1M (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5M, for agreements entered into from March 20, 2025 to 2031. The older GST New Housing Rebate covers homes the FTHB rebate does not: 36% of the GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.

Presales and new completions: REDMA gives a 7-day rescission period under s. 21 and requires purchase deposits to be held in trust under s. 18 — the framework for developer contracts at Gabriel and any remaining developer inventory at Galilea and Quinn.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queen Mary Park Surrey

items.t: The neighbourhood is named for a park most listings over-describe: the City's own page for Queen Mary Park lists trails, a playground and the Healy Creek ecosystem — and does not list the gardens, picnic areas or sports facilities that appear in marketing copy for the area.

One building in the southern cluster cannot be honestly named in these notes: the condo building at 8183 121A Street is real (a current listing index confirms the address and type), but its name, storeys and build year exist only on a source these notes do not cite — so it is carried as not confirmed and uncounted rather than named on a single weak source.

Eclipse is the opposite case — a name with a paper trail: Surrey Council minutes from 2006 and 2007 record the four-storey apartment building approved at 8084 120A Street, so the building's existence and form rest on a City primary source even though its build year and unit count stay not confirmed.

The northern cluster is a two-developer story: Porte built Quinn (174 units, 2024), and Whitetail built Galilea (129 homes) and Gabriel (125 condos) side by side on the same 94A/95 Avenue ground — Galilea's sales centre served both projects, so early Gabriel buyers were sold from inside Galilea.

Quinn's own directory presence contains a trap: a "22-unit development" header attached to its 9456 134 Street address contradicts the project's documented 174 units — a per-page directory figure that should never be quoted as the building's size.
The two halves of this small sub-area do not behave alike.

There is no Queen Mary Park Elementary anchoring this neighbourhood record — the name comes from the City park, and the elementary schools on the Ministry list for this ground are David Brankin, Senator Reid, Betty Huff, Kennedy Trail and Kirkbride.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queen Mary Park

items.t: The park the area is named for is smaller in the City's telling than in listing copy.

Two "Lakewood" names, two different sub-areas, opposite age rules. Lakewood Grove (8257 121A St, this sub-area) shows no age restriction in any source checked, while Lakewood Place and Lakewood Heights on W Boundary Drive (Panorama Ridge) are verified 55+ townhouses. A name-based alert mixes them.

The townhouse stock is old, and that is the diligence story. Five of the seven counted complexes date from 1974–1991 on their verified records (Bonnydoon Village 1974, Barkerville II 1988, Hadley Green 1989, Lakewood Grove 1991, Kennedy Trail 2008 the exception) — depreciation reports and CRF balances matter more here than in Surrey's newer townhouse pockets.

No City plan area stands behind the name. "Queen Mary Park" is a board sub-area and a park name, not a City planning district — City documents for this ground are filed under Whalley / City Centre and Newton framings, so a search run under only the board name misses them.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

44 townhomes sold in Queen Mary Park with a median price of $669,000 (the middle half sold between $614,975 and $725,750), taking a median of 38 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 14% sold above list. They had a median $455 per square foot, a median year built of 1988 and a median strata fee of $351 a month. 36 condos sold in Queen Mary Park with a median price of $436,500 (the middle half sold between $367,500 and $530,500), taking a median of 44 days to sell at 96.3% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $513 per square foot, a median year built of 1996 and a median strata fee of $416 a month.

faq.a: Levies and the depreciation report. Every strata of five or more lots must renew its report every five years since July 1, 2024; at 50 years old, envelope, roofing and plumbing items dominate.
